findings.description: typescript-source.utils.ts imports a .client.ts module and does impure execFileSync I/O, breaking the utils role's 'pure functions only' contract.
findings.body:
`docs/conventions/naming.md` line 76 states the `utils` role's contract without exception: **"Pure functions only. Cannot import `service`, `manager`, `repository`, or `client`. If it needs one of those, it isn't a util."**

This PR adds [`import { GIT_SAFE_CONFIG, scrubbedGitEnv } from '../core/git-diff.client.js';`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/cc13ad914ec1828e43e7b0806269f6190cb74cd3/src/adapters/typescript-source.utils.ts#L3) to `typescript-source.utils.ts`, and the new `committedPackageDirs` directly shells out via [`execFileSync('git', ...)`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/cc13ad914ec1828e43e7b0806269f6190cb74cd3/src/adapters/typescript-source.utils.ts#L100-L124) — genuine impure child-process I/O, not a pure function. Before this PR the file only imported `node:path` helpers and contained zero I/O; this diff is what introduces the violation (confirmed against the diff, not pre-existing code that moved).

`src/cli/project.utils.ts` already does the same thing, but that's a pre-existing violation of the same rule elsewhere in the repo, not a documented exception — nothing in decision 31, 32, or the new decision 58 carves out an exception for adapters that need to shell out to git for trust-boundary reasons. The rule's own text names the fix: move `nestedPackageDirs`/`committedPackageDirs` into a differently-suffixed module (e.g. `.client.ts`), since a file that needs `client`-level capability isn't a util.

findings.description: This test comment ('Decision 58: a directory with its own package.json has its own runner...') restates nestedPackageDirs's own JSDoc and is immediately redundant with the two it() names right below it — nothing is lost if it's deleted, per AGENTS.md's rule against a call-site WHY comment duplicating the callee's seam.

This test comment ('Nothing diffs or hashes an untracked file in the main checkout...') is a near-verbatim duplicate of nestedPackageDirs's JSDoc in typescript-source.utils.ts ('an untracked src/core/package.json dropped into the main checkout from a session shell is diffed and hashed by nothing'), which AGENTS.md's comment rule treats as a duplicate to delete.

This test comment ('The main checkout's index is a session's to git add to...') is a near-verbatim duplicate of language in both nestedPackageDirs's JSDoc and decision 58's own text in docs/09-decisions.md — the seam already says it, so per AGENTS.md the call-site copy should be deleted.

withoutFiles's JSDoc ('The report without the files `excluded` names.') restates the signature instead of carrying a WHY, unlike the sibling repoCoverageRatio doc two lines above it which states a genuine gotcha (undefined when nothing is instrumented) — general.md's JSDoc rule asks for the latter.

The second commit's message opens with 'Security review of 3aef43e', but 3aef43e isn't a resolvable object in this repo's history — the PR's actual first commit is b5c43be. Likely a stale hash left over from local iteration before squashing/rebasing; harmless but worth a glance before merge.

process_issues.description: One correctness instance's sandbox blocked ad-hoc `node -e` spikes it wanted to run to double-check isInNestedPackage edge cases; it fell back to static reading only and reported no change to its conclusions.

`gh pr diff 103` initially hit a sandbox output-redirection restriction for the conventions reviewer; it substituted `git diff <merge-base>..HEAD` and confirmed identical content, so the review itself was not degraded.
